Animal Walk Parade

Children move like different animals across a room or play space.

Modifications included
Best for
Toddlers, Preschoolers, School-age children
Season
All year
Place
Indoors, Outdoors
Time
10 min
Children
1-20
Adults
1
You will need
Not specified
View activity

How it works

Children copy animal-inspired movements such as bear walks, frog jumps, and crab walks.

Steps

Choose 3 to 5 animals, demonstrate each movement, then invite children to move from one side of the space to the other.

Safety notes

Keep the area clear, avoid slippery surfaces, and invite children to move at a comfortable speed.

Participation support

Children using mobility aids can choose upper-body animal actions, animal sounds, facial expressions, or partner-led movements.

Make it easier

Use fewer animals and shorter distances.

Make it harder

Add movement cards or ask children to create their own animal movement.

Reviewed: April 25, 2026

Bubble Pop Reach

Children reach, stretch, step, or roll to pop bubbles blown by an adult.

Designed for broad participation
Best for
Infants, Toddlers, Preschoolers
Season
Spring, Summer
Place
Outdoors
Time
10 min
Children
1-15
Adults
1
You will need
Bubbles
View activity

How it works

An adult blows bubbles while children move to reach and pop them.

Steps

Blow bubbles at different heights and distances while encouraging safe reaching, stepping, rolling, or pointing.

Safety notes

Use non-toxic bubble solution, avoid blowing bubbles directly into faces, and watch for slippery ground.

Participation support

Adjust bubble height, distance, and pace for each child. Children can point, clap, track with their eyes, or pop bubbles with a preferred movement.

Make it easier

Keep bubbles close to the child and use slower bubble streams.

Make it harder

Ask children to pop bubbles using elbows, knees, feet, or a chosen body part.

Reviewed: April 25, 2026

Freeze Dance

Children dance while music plays and freeze when the music stops.

Season
All year
Place
Indoors
Time
12 min
Children
2-30
Adults

You will need
Music player
View activity

How it works

Children move creatively to music and practice stopping when the music pauses.

Steps

Play music for short bursts, pause it, and invite children to freeze in place until the music starts again.

Safety notes

Use a clear open area and keep the volume comfortable.

Participation support

Children can freeze with any body part, gesture, facial expression, seated pose, or supported standing pose.

Make it easier

Use slower music and longer pauses.

Make it harder

Add themed poses, balance shapes, leader turns, or rhythm changes.

Reviewed: April 25, 2026

Obstacle Path

Children move through a simple path using cones, hoops, tape lines, or cushions.

Modifications included
Best for
Preschoolers, School-age children
Season
All year
Place
Indoors, Outdoors
Time
15 min
Children
2-20
Adults
2
You will need
Cones, hoops, tape lines, or cushions
View activity

How it works

Children practice balance, coordination, and movement planning through a short obstacle path.

Steps

Create 4 to 6 stations such as step over, crawl around, balance line, and jump spot. Invite children to move through one at a time.

Safety notes

Keep obstacles low, stable, and spaced apart. Avoid hard edges and crowded paths.

Participation support

Offer alternate routes, wider paths, seated stations, visual cues, or partner support.

Make it easier

Remove stations and use a straight path with one movement at a time.

Make it harder

Add teamwork, child-designed stations, or a memory challenge.

Reviewed: April 25, 2026

Scarf Toss and Catch

Children toss lightweight scarves and try to catch them before they land.

Designed for broad participation
Best for
Infants, Toddlers, Preschoolers
Season
All year
Place
Indoors
Time
8 min
Children
1-12
Adults
1
You will need
Lightweight scarves
View activity

How it works

Children practice tracking, reaching, throwing, and catching with soft scarves.

Steps

Give each child one scarf. Invite them to toss it upward, watch it fall, and catch it with hands, arms, or lap.

Safety notes

Use soft scarves only and provide enough spacing between children.

Participation support

Use larger scarves, slower tosses, seated play, or adult hand-over-hand support when helpful.

Make it easier

Let the scarf drop into hands or onto a lap instead of catching in the air.

Make it harder

Add claps, turns, body-part catches, or partner tosses.

Reviewed: April 25, 2026

Seasonal Treasure Walk

Children look for safe seasonal items or picture cards during a guided walk.

Modifications included
Best for
Toddlers, Preschoolers, School-age children
Season
Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter
Place
Outdoors
Time
20 min
Children
2-25
Adults

You will need

View activity

How it works

Children walk through an outdoor area searching for leaves, cones, colours, shapes, or laminated picture cards.

Steps

Set a short route, explain what children are looking for, and pause often so children can point, collect, or describe what they find.

Safety notes

Avoid unsafe plants, sharp objects, traffic areas, and extreme weather.

Participation support

Use picture cards at reachable heights, provide seated observation spots, or pair children with a buddy.

Make it easier

Use fewer items and a shorter route.

Make it harder

Add counting, sorting, matching, or child-led clue giving.

Reviewed: April 25, 2026
